model.name: First key toggles native keyboard while RETAINING the artificial key bar (input-accessory retention, device-only) — extends R40.3
model.description: The FIRST (leftmost/primary) key on the artificial key bar TOGGLES the native keyboard shown vs hidden, and the artificial keys action bar STAYS VISIBLE AND USABLE IN BOTH states (input-accessory style — sits ABOVE the keyboard when shown, never covered/unmounted). Input still reaches the PTY in both states (R40.3 anti-vacuity holds); terminal stays visible per R40.3 pixel ACs; the key is an action unit (R40.5). DEVICE-ONLY real iOS @390 (a headless browser cannot show/hide an iOS keyboard). ★ CHANGES R40.3's SHAPE: keyboard suppression becomes a SETTABLE STATE owned by the bar (re-enableable), NOT a bolt-on fighting by-construction suppression.
model.tronQuote: the first button on the artificial action line keys is toggle between native keyboard hidden and shown while retaining the keys action bar
model.crossRefNote: EXTENDS + RE-SHAPES R40.3 (suppress-OS-keyboard): suppression must become a SETTABLE STATE owned by the bar so it is re-enableable/toggleable — architect must not let it be a bolt-on. Reuses R40.3 anti-vacuity (input-reaches-PTY) + pixel ACs + device-B split; R40.5 action-unit.

discoverySource.note: Extends R40.3. HARD PART = RETENTION (bar above the iOS keyboard, input-accessory, never covered) = the AC most likely to fail on-device while passing headless. DESIGN-REQUIRED: R40.3 shape-change (suppression = settable state owned by the bar, re-enableable). Device-only real-iOS @390 (headless cannot show/hide iOS keyboard).

acceptanceCriteria.text: The FIRST (leftmost/primary) key on the artificial key bar IS the toggle — the POSITION is part of the requirement, not a detail.
Firing it TOGGLES the native (iOS) soft keyboard between SHOWN and HIDDEN.

★ THE HARD AC (device, most likely to fail-on-device while passing headless): the artificial keys action bar is RETAINED and USABLE in BOTH states. With the native keyboard SHOWN the bar must sit ABOVE the keyboard (input-accessory style) — never covered, never unmounted.
Input STILL REACHES THE PTY in BOTH states — R40.3's anti-vacuity AC still holds. A bar that renders but sends nothing is the empty-container class we fixed twice this session.
The terminal remains visible/usable per R40.3's pixel ACs (in both keyboard states).
The toggle key is an ACTION UNIT per R40.5's de-duplication — never a bespoke button.
★ DEVICE-ONLY: verified on real iOS @390 on Tron's device, NEVER headless-green. A headless browser cannot show or hide an iOS soft keyboard — the same reason R40.3-B was already split device-only.

★ DESIGN-REQUIRED (architect, R40.3 SHAPE-CHANGE): R40.3 suppressed the keyboard BY CONSTRUCTION; a toggle requires suppression to be a SETTABLE STATE OWNED BY THE BAR (re-enableable), NOT a bolt-on that fights the by-construction suppression. This changes R40.3's shape, not just adds to it.
